text: The biopsy findings of nuclear hyperchromasia and multinucleation are classic for koilocytosis, which is pathognomonic for HPV infection, despite the negative DNA test which may be a false negative or due to variant strains. Given the clinical presentation of verrucous, non-healing lesions on the penis and finger in an older male, this is highly suggestive of Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (Giant Condyloma Acuminatum), which is an aggressive, locally destructive form of condyloma acuminatum with potential for malignant transformation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Buschke-Löwenstein tumor (Giant Condyloma Acuminatum)
